relations.subject: sso:realm
relations.evidence:
Choose to turn on or off group mapping.  
Group mapping allows you to assign roles to SSO users based on which teams map to their SSO group.

relations.subject: sso:realm
relations.evidence:
Choose a default team.  
Capella automatically assigns users to the chosen default team when they do not match any team based on their SSO groups.

notable_absence.finding: Prerequisite gate is a linked but generic term - 'as an [Account Owner](https://onelogin.service-now.com/support?...)' - same shape as sso-google.md's linked 'super administrator'; contrast the unlinked CyberArk/Okta/Ping wording and the specific, named sso-entra-id.md 'Global Administrator'.

cross_component_finding: OneLogin's OIDC configuration is the only one of the six providers with an extra manual step not mirrored anywhere else in the batch: 'Change the Token Endpoint Authentication Method to POST.' Ping's OIDC flow has an analogous but differently-valued step ('Change the Token Endpoint Authentication Method to Client Secret Post'), while CyberArk, Google Workspace, Entra ID, and Okta's OIDC flows never mention a token endpoint authentication method setting at all. Since all four use the same underlying 'Client ID'/'Client Secret' realm fields, this suggests either a real default-value difference between IdPs that only two provider guides happen to surface, or an inconsistency in how thoroughly each guide documents the same underlying OIDC client requirement - worth a coordinator follow-up, potentially a docs-issue if Capella's OIDC realm actually requires a specific token endpoint auth method regardless of IdP.
